moments.title: Lockout and private guards
moments.facts: Henry Frick locked out workers and brought about 300 Pinkerton agents to guard the mill. A violent clash followed; the Pennsylvania militia later took control of the area, and the company reopened with replacement workers.
moments.interpretation: Private force helped the company regain the mill; the strike failed, and the response damaged its public reputation.
moments.difference: Pinkerton agents were used as guards here. Detective agencies also conducted undercover labor investigations, a related but distinct practice.

moments.title: Workers strike to organize
moments.facts: Workers at Carnegie Steel's Homestead Works struck in a dispute over organizing. The lockout and attempt to secure the mill escalated into a violent confrontation.
moments.interpretation: The employer's refusal to accept worker organization turned a labor dispute into a contest over who controlled the workplace.
moments.difference: The current game event records a walkout; it does not imply that an armed confrontation or lockout will follow.
